name: Claude-Code-Game-Studios
description: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio — 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.
one_liner: Turns a single Claude Code chat into a simulated game studio, with dozens of specialist AI 'roles' (designer, programmer, QA, artist) that review each other's work so a solo person's game project stays organized instead of turning into a mess of hardcoded hacks.
buyer: A solo or small-team indie game developer who already uses Claude Code and wants their AI-built game project to have design docs, QA passes, and structure instead of accumulating spaghetti code.
business_use_cases: A solo indie dev uses it to force a design-doc-first, reviewed workflow on their game project so scope and code quality don't collapse after a few weeks of solo vibe-coding.
A tiny 2-3 person indie studio adopts it as a shared process so AI-assisted contributions from different people stay consistent and get the same 'QA lead' and 'creative director' review gates.
A game-dev educator or YouTuber uses it as a teaching framework to show students how a real studio's roles and review gates work, using AI agents to play each role.

money_ideas.idea: It's free and open (MIT), funded via Buy Me a Coffee/GitHub Sponsors donations rather than a product sale.
A developer could sell paid custom agent/skill packs tailored to a specific engine or genre (e.g. a roguelike-specific QA/balance agent set) as an add-on.

steal_this: Pick one small game prototype you've been putting off, run it entirely through this studio template for a weekend, and ship a devlog about the experience — the content itself (not the template) is the sellable thing, since the repo is free and donation-funded.
